messages:
carmen_sales: Heads upAcme SRE on the POC can't stitch traces together. They see requests across multiple services with no common id. Demo tomorrow morning. Any chance we can wire trace ids to Datadog quickly? @sam_soleng @li_engineer
sam_soleng: Are they using our Hosted API or Dedicated infra? That changes forwarder setup and whether we can change ingress rules.
acme_sre: Hosted SDK + our sidecar. We do send `x-request-id` from client, but responses don't return it and the dd logs show no `request_id` attribute.
li_engineer: OK. Most likely missing header passthrough and our log forwarder mapping. Quick checklist: 1) ensure ingress proxies forward `x-request-id`, 2) runtime emits `request_id`/`trace_id` fields, 3) forwarder map to `request_id` in Datadog.
ops_bot: Created ticket INF-8891 and provisioned ephemeral forwarder ff:acme-staging -> https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/acme-staging (status: provisioning) :gear:
sam_soleng: Carmen, can you paste a sample curl showing headers? Also need org id for per-org flags.
carmen_sales: sample: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk:acme-demo" -H "X-Request-ID: rq-71f" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat`
li_engineer: Good. I'll flip the per-org tracing flag for acme-org in staging: `enable_request_tracing=true` and add the header passthrough rule to the ingress route.
acme_sre: Would we need any changes to our sidecar? We're running envoy with http1 upstream.
li_engineer: Envoy should pass through by default, but some of our internal proxies rebuild headers. I'll run a header-trace: `kubectl exec -c curl pod/foo -- curl -v -H 'X-Request-ID: test-42' http://svc-internal` to confirm.
sam_soleng: Also FYI Acme asked about whether tracing data will contain PII. Security questionnaire item: "Do traces include request payloads?" We should answer: runtime may emit metadata and trace ids; payloads are not stored in traces by default. I'll loop in security doc.
ops_bot: Forwarder provisioning complete: ff-7432 (active). Logs now streaming to acme-staging.
li_engineer: I patched ingress rule: `proxy_set_header X-Request-ID $http_x_request_id;` and restarted the route. Also pushed a small runtime feature toggle for `request_id_in_response=true` for acme-org.
acme_sre: Testing nowI see response header `X-Request-ID: rq-71f` echoed back. Datadog logs show some entries with `request_id`, but not all.
li_engineer: Which services missing it? Can you grep for requests without request_id? Example query: `logs('source:api AND !request_id').limit(100)`
carmen_sales: They reported missing ones from "batcher" and "router" services.
li_engineer: Batcher historically rewrites headers for aggregated requests. I'll add code to copy `x-request-id` into the internal RPC metadata: patch PR inbound.
sam_soleng: Meanwhile I'll create a minimal DD dashboard they can use for the demo: widgets for 429s by `request_id`, average latency per `request_id`, and a top-list of services dropping the id. I'll paste JSON once sanitized.
acme_sre: Also saw lots of 429s from parallel test. Could we temporarily increase trial rate limits? It's blocking their end-to-end test.
li_engineer: Yes, can bump trial token limits for acme-org to 200 RPS for 30 minutes. Doing now.
ops_bot: Rate limit override applied for org acme-org: 200rps (expires in 30m).
acme_sre: Re-run tests: now the request flow shows request_id across services and Datadog groups traces correctly. 429s are minimal. Dashboard looks good. Thanks! :tada:
carmen_sales: Amazing. Action items: (1) Add quick doc "Request ID & Tracing for Hosted POCs" with steps and troubleshooting, (2) default-enable echoing `X-Request-ID` for Hosted, (3) add ingress integration test in CI to prevent regressions. @sam_soleng can you take (1) and (2)?
sam_soleng: I'll draft the doc and a sanitized dashboard JSON. I'll open a tracking ticket to default-enable echoing and add the CI test. ETA: EOD tomorrow.
li_engineer: I'll follow up with a small PR to batcher to preserve headers and a runbook snippet for debug commands.
acme_sre: One last note: security asked whether logs forwarded to Datadog are encrypted in transit and retained per our policy. We confirmed TLS to Datadog and retention per contract.
sam_soleng: I'll attach the relevant security blurb in the doc.
carmen_sales: Closing the loopthanks everyone for the quick swarm!
